newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Koh Brothers unit gets nod for listing.
newsitem.headline: Koh Brothers unit gets nod for listing.

text.p: Construction firm Koh Brothers Group Ltd said on Thursday its G&W Group (Holdings) Pte Ltd unit would list on the mainboard of the Stock Exchange of Singapore.
"We expect the listing to take place in about a month's time," Tiak Chye Koh, managing director of Koh Brothers, told a news conference.
Koh had said in October 1996 the group planned to list its units in the future.
A prospectus for an initial public offering of G&W shares would be published in the near future, Koh said.
No details of the number of shares or the proposed offer price were disclosed, but Koh said G&W aimed to raise between Singapore $10 million to S$15 million from the offering.
"We believe the opportunities are now really right for us to be able to expand our business," Alan Tan, G&W group general manager, told reporters.

Singapore-based G&W currently has operations in China, Indonesia and Malaysia and no plans at this stage to expand its geographic spread, but would seek to boost its share in existing markets, Tan said.
"We want to expand our business in the region, starting off with Malaysia later this year," he added.
G&W is involved in making ready-mixed concrete -- which accounts for about 80 percent of its turnover -- pre-cast concrete and renting construction equipment.
Expanding its pump rental business, which "has got the highest growth" of all, was a priority that would begin in Malaysia in the third quarter of the year, Tan said.
G&W contributes about 30 to 40 percent of Koh Brothers profits and about 40 to 50 percent of the group's turnover.
G&W reported pretax profits of S$5 million in 1996 on turnover of S$97 million.
The company has experienced compounded annual growth from 1992 of 63 percent from S$0.7 million for profits and 23 percent from S$45 million for turnover.
